verified_fact: On June 21, 2001, BHP Billiton ran an iron ore train in Western Australia measuring 7.353 km with 682 wagons and 8 GE AC6000CW locomotives, weighing 99,734 tonnes.
voiceover_script: Imagine karo ek aisi train jo 7.3 kilometer lambi hai! Itni lambi ki engine se aakhri dibba dekhne ke liye binoculars chahiye. Ye hai Australia ke Pilbara registan mein chalne wali BHP Iron Ore Train. 21 June 2001 ko is train ne duniya ki sabse lambi aur sabse bhaari train ka official record banaya tha. Is akeli train ko chalane ke liye 8 vishal GE diesel locomotives lagaye gaye the. Har engine 6,000 horsepower deta hai, matlab kul milakar 48,000 horsepower ki taakat! Lekin ye aathon engine aage nahi jude the. Train ko patri se utarne se bachane ke liye engines ko do-do ke jodon mein poori 7 kilometer ki lambai mein baanta gaya tha, jo radio signals se synchronize hote the. Isme kul 682 wagons the, jinme 82,000 ton iron ore bhara tha. Train ka total wazan lagbhag 1 lakh ton tha! Agar ye train kisi crossing se 70 km/h par guzre, toh use poora cross hone mein 6 se 7 minute lagte hain. Port Hedland pahunch kar special rotary dumpers bina dibbe alag kiye unhe ulta karke ore khali karte the. 2001 ke baad aaj tak kisi ne aisi train dobara nahi chalayi. Kya India mein Dedicated Freight Corridor par aisi lambi train chal sakti hai?
